anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer repeatedly chooses or reuses an execution plan whose estimated cost is far lower than its actual execution cost, despite reasonably accurate statistics, leading to inefficient operator choices or join orders.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: Critical depletion of free space in data, log, or temporary storage areas causes allocation failures, auto‐extension stalls, and log‐archive back-pressure, threatening normal read/write activity.

Composite definition: This anomaly represents the simultaneous presence of a sub-optimal execution plan and an imminent or ongoing exhaustion of storage space. The workload must cope with an inefficient plan while the underlying storage subsystem approaches or reaches hard space limits.

Combined observable phenomena: Queries may flip from index access to full table scans or large hash joins that generate unexpectedly large spill files; these spills hit nearly full temporary tablespaces, producing "out of space" errors or forcing repeated chunk allocations that thrash I/O. Poor plans expand rowset sizes, inflate undo/redo volume, and prolong transaction duration; at the same time free space for logs and archives shrinks, causing checkpoint slowdowns, log switch waits, and even halt of DML once logs cannot be recycled. Operators see both elevated CPU/elapsed time and sudden space-related error messages. Monitoring shows plan changes, runaway temp usage, rapid growth of data/log files, and blocked sessions waiting on space reclamation or manual extension.

Causal interaction: A bad plan often materializes or spills far more intermediate data than a well-chosen plan, rapidly consuming temp and log space and accelerating the onset of capacity limits. Conversely, when space is already scarce, the optimizer may reject or be unable to create certain plan shapes (e.g., parallel hash join requiring temp segments) and settle on alternative but inferior plans, reinforcing the selection anomaly. Capacity exhaustion can also invalidate or flush cached plans, provoking re-optimization and further plan instability. The two root causes therefore reinforce each other: the sub-optimal plan intensifies space consumption, and the constrained space environment biases the optimizer toward even less efficient plans, together degrading throughput and risking service outages.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that takes more than the specified amount of time; zero disables the timeout.
entry.trigger_condition: A SQL statement runs longer than statement_timeout, measured from command arrival until completion.
entry.workload_impact: The running statement is aborted; when configured, the timed-out statement is logged.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
